rationale: C10 plausibly supplied a material template because it delegates a presidential function concerning the determination of “critical defense-housing areas” to the Director of Defense Mobilization—the same specialized subject and one of the same delegatees used in the child. The child adapts that machinery to powers newly conferred by the Housing and Rent Act of 1953 and requires joint action with the Secretary of Defense. C14 is also close through its delegation of “all powers, duties, and functions” under the same Housing and Rent Act, while C12 provides a similar compact single-sentence delegation form, but neither matches C10’s distinctive combination of critical defense housing and the Director of Defense Mobilization.

shared_material.child_excerpt: relating to critical defense housing areas, to the Secretary of Defense and the Director of Defense Mobilization
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Director of Defense Mobilization is hereby designated and empowered to perform ... the function vested in the President ... of determining critical defense-housing areas
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive overlap in both the specialized administrative target and the designated official supports reuse beyond generic delegation boilerplate.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I hereby delegate all powers, duties, and functions conferred upon the President
shared_material.parent_excerpt: designated and empowered to perform, without the approval, ratification, or other action of the president, the function vested in the President
shared_material.explanation: Both use presidential delegation machinery to transfer statutorily vested defense-housing functions for direct performance by an executive official.
